sites.quote: However, since the Opaque LSA type defines the flooding scope, the LSA flooding scope MUST satisfy the application-specific requirements for all the prefixes included in a single OSPFv2 Extended Prefix Opaque LSA.
If the flag is set and the prefix length is not a host prefix, then the flag MUST be ignored.
Only one OSPFv2 Extended Link TLV SHALL be advertised in each OSPFv2 Extended Link Opaque LSA, allowing for fine granularity changes in the topology.
However, future OSPFv2 applications utilizing these extensions MUST address backward compatibility of the corresponding functionality.
Malformed LSAs MUST NOT be stored in the Link State Database (LSDB), acknowledged, or reflooded.
Types in the range 32768-33023 are for Experimental Use; these will not be registered with IANA and MUST NOT be mentioned by RFCs.
